subtitle: A "regression" that's actually the classic yes/no classifier.

eyebrow: Why not just use a line?

code:
logit = 2.0 - 0.09 * tenure   # true relationship
clf = LogisticRegression().fit(X_tr, y_tr)
print(clf.intercept_.round(2), clf.coef_.round(3))
# [2.35]  [[-0.107]]  -- close to the built-in 2.0, -0.09
caption: LogisticRegression applies L2 regularization by default -- part of why it's not an exact match.

code:
clf.predict_proba([[6], [36]]).round(2)
# [[0.15 0.85]     <- 6 months: 85% churn risk
#  [0.82 0.18]]    <- 36 months: 18% churn risk
clf.predict([[6], [36]])   # [True, False] -- default threshold 0.5
caption: Lower the threshold to catch more churners -- at the cost of more false alarms.

code:
accuracy_score(y_te, clf.predict(X_te))   # 0.79
confusion_matrix(y_te, clf.predict(X_te))
# [[52  9]   <- 61 stayed: 52 right, 9 flagged wrongly
#  [12 27]]  <- 39 churned: 27 caught, 12 missed
caption: Rows = actual class, columns = predicted. The basis for precision, recall, and more.

eyebrow: The S-curve, fit to real data
caption: Crosses the 0.5 threshold at about 22 months of tenure.

eyebrow: Reading a coefficient: odds, not probability
caption: Each extra month multiplies churn ODDS by ~0.90 -- a ~10% reduction, holding others fixed.
